reviews.comment: doc is the goat and he is very kind and encourages you to ask questions so even if the class is hard just ask questions and you'll be happy and he would be happy because you're asking questions. And he even ran 4 president. the class itself is pretty chill mostly CTF homeworks. THX

Dr. Carlisle is funny and cares a lot for his students. Complete homeworks as soon as you can because they can take a while, but exams are easy as long as you review the contents and understand how the homework problems are solved. Practice, and you'll be fine. It's a very insightful class and Carlisle as a lot to show for it.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class isn't as easy as the other professor, but I would say the overall difficulty is fair. Homeworks took slightly longer but they are harder than the exam questions. I would practice the homework problems (and similar problems) for exam review. Quizzes are fine but some are tricky. Also recommend to watch his short videos before class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I went to every lecture but didn't learn much. Had to rely on ChatGPT to learn everything. HW takes hours every week and has to be done in latex. He gives quizzes every week over the last week's material. Exams are graded harshly, but there's a good chance you can get some points back by explaining your reasoning to a TA in office hours

Everything I learned came from either the textbook or Youtube. He just goes over examples as if we already know stuff and just repeats the same thing slowly when asked for an explanation. The worst part is that all of his HW is to be done using Latex, which took hours for me to type up, a flat 0 for showing any written work. Exam grading is HARSH

I wouldn't say he is that good of a lecturer. Grading is quite tough on quizzes, homework. There are quizzes every other class. The content itself isn't that bad but when he teaches it in class, it just makes it worse. When I watch his videos on canvas, I am more confused after than before. Goes very fast in class, expecting us to alr know it all.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice guy and all, decent teacher, but he grades like a mf. Like I wouldn't recommend, but I also wouldn't not recommend him.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He only does example questions in class, so read ahead. Super nice grader with partial credit, very encouraging & friendly & clear expectations. No surprise quizzes or HW's; HW is harder than the tests, but still study (1st test is the hardest). He knew everyone's name by the 2-3rd week. I enjoyed his class & will take him again if I get the option
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Grading is brutal. The professor forces TAs to take off massive points for silly mistakes. The homework is extremely time consuming, so be realistic and expect a B. The material is tough, but the lectures make it worse. The instruction is very confusing and goes very fast, and sitting in class honestly feels like listening to a foreign language.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All I'm going to say for this rating: I'm building my future schedule around taking more of Doc's classes. This guy is literally the best professor I've ever had.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had heard great things, but Dr.Carlisle did not feel like a great lecturer. I felt extremely confused as he glossed over topics quickly, and would not spend much time on practice problems. Homework + in class quiz every week, so constantly studying and not falling behind on material is a must. Not a bad professor, but did not work for me.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: best 222 prof. weekly hw (12) and quizzes (10), 2 of each dropped. hw is easy (2ish hrs), quizzes are 25 pts and 2-3 questions, there is partial credit, and questions are similar to lecture and hw questions. 2 exams + final, exams are similar to practice exams he posts and hw questions. no practice for final. i only went to class for the quiz
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very kind professor who does try to make time for his students. His grading system is very forgiving, but don't expect to be able to coast through the class without learning the material. I think his lectures tend to be a little confusing, so expect to do most of your learning outside of class. The homeworks are the hardest part of the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very engaging lecturer, but some concepts were hard to understand. If you do the homeworks, they are harder than the exams and you should be able to get an a.

Dr. Carlisle is an engaging lecturer but tends to let the lecture get derailed on loosely related tangents and personal anecdotes or entertaining the frequent and oftentimes entirely unrelated questions posed by a few very vocal students. I enjoyed the class & Doc, but I feel I didn't learn as much as I could have if the lectures were more focused.

CSCE 465 (software reverse engineering) was an interesting class, and probably is less structured than some of Doc's other classes are.  The majority of the grade came from solving CTF questions, which was really fun. I have no complaints and I feel like I learned a lot.

Sometimes I found it hard to keep up with his lectures, but at the end of the day, the way he organized this class made it very simple to get an A.  You definitely have to put in the effort to study outside of class.  The homework was the hardest part of the class.  Quizzes and exams were easy - often only covering the simplest practice problems.

Dr. Carlisle is an amazing prof who is extremely intelligent. I loved going to his lectures because it gave a lot of good insight for the course. Now, the material is pretty heavy so of course you need to do some studying on your own (like very minor it's not bad). Quizzes and exams are easier than the homework so no worries there.

Professor Carlilse's lectures were pretty hard to follow since he went very fast and didn't stop much if students had questions. Quizzes and Midterms were pretty easy but the Final was a lot more difficult. Doesn't offer much extra credit but is a light grader for the most part.

Dr. Carlisle's lectures proved challenging to follow. Instead of explaining concepts, he swiftly skimmed through practice problems which students were not prepared for leaving them confused and requiring self teaching. However, he was accessible in office hours and would clear up confusion after class. Exams and quizzes were super easy.

Dr. Carslie is an amazing professor. From his teaching style to all of the jokes and stories he uses to explain complex topics in class, straight up amazing. I highly recommend him for this class and you will not be disappointed.
Great guy. Extremely smart but will slow down if you have questions. Always came to class happy. This course is tough, so you have to pay attention and go to class.

Doc's class was the only class I actually wanted to attend this semester, his lectures motivate you to stay and learn the concepts. He goes over them very thoroughly and when you ask questions he gives very helpful responses. The only thing I would say that he falls short on is that when we are learning something new, he skips over crucial steps.

In his lectures he goes by super fast but I swear if you just sit and think about the content its rly easy. HW is harder but there are resources in the textbook that help a lot. His final was drop dead easy - his tests are easy in general but study for exam 1. You use this class for the rest of your CS career so make sure you understand the content

This class is going to be the extremely hard no matter who you have but at least doc will take the time to help you through it. compared to the other professors of 222, hes your best prof by far. The weekly homework is hard but not impossible, tests are usually the simplest version of each concept, hes not trying to tick you or fail you.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Doc is a really amazing professor, but do not expect much sympathy. This class is not traditionally difficult, but the grading scheme is very harsh and if you mess up much on the first test you can expect to not get an A. Doc is a very good lecturer. Make sure you find the best TA and go to their office hours. Before tests.

You will immediately be able to tell that doc is a smart guy. My only complaint is that I would very often get lost in the lectures, but this could be fixed by the videos that he put out and the textbook.

Doc is a pretty good lecturer, but what makes him the best is his availability and desire to help students learn. If you put in the effort, you will do well. Material isn't too tough. Attending and participating in lecture makes it easier.

He isn't the worst professor. He teaches decently but he goes too fast for me. And he has class favorites who he only interacts with. Other than that he only does practice problems which are hard to follow along. His grading is fair but the final had 50% of its question come from the last 2 units. Messed me up! homeworks are hard!
His lectures made the programming assignments doable. I routinely based my schedule around asking him for help. He is fantastic and a great prof.

Doc is probably the best prof u can get for 222. Homeworks take forever; coded through LaTeX. Easy 5 hrs a week and tedious. Get ready to read because Doc only goes over examples in class that are "similar" to HW. Doc also has a problem of not explaining things in different ways if ur confused. He says what he said originally, just slower. EZ B
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Carlisle is GOATed, he the real MVP frfr. The homeworks were very interactive and fun at times, and was always receptive to questions regarding the homework, lecture, or anything Cybersecurity related. Highly recommend taking him for 465, hes the best prof for the course, and arguably top 3 prof in the department.

Super intelligent and excellent professor. His lectures are clear and example heavy. His homework aren't for the faint of heart, but he's accessible outside of class, and has helped make discrete math my favorite class this semester.

Easily my favorite professor at TAMU. He cares about his students, has fun and engaging lectures, and is intelligent out of his mind. Ask questions often and go to office hours - one-on-one help is a game-changer and he's fun to learn and hear from. Material/work is not for the faint of heart, but he's willing to give you the help you need.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor, spent hours working on codes and trying to fix them. Go to his office hours, he is a great lecturer and very good about giving precise examples.
He simplifies the toughest concepts to the greatest extent. The homework and the projects are also challenging but you get to learn a lot while doing them.

CSCE 489 was the second time I've taken a class with Dr. Carlisle, and I think he is one of the best professors, if not the best, in the C.S. department. He cares about making connections with his students and making sure you learn. He'll make you work for your grade, but if you follow instructions, you'll pass his classes with flying colors.

Dr. Carlisle is the only reason I passed this class. It was super hard, but he was extremely helpful in office hours. He definitely cares for his students and I am grateful for all the materials he provided to assist in surviving 121. Definitely the best professor for the course even though it is supposed to be standardized.

Knowledgeable professor who clearly enjoys his job; in CSCE 120/121 at least his teaching style was more interactive involving the students doing their own coding and whatnot; very open to questions and student interaction. I do personally wish we could have more concrete information sources though other than the book which isn't very thorough

Taking CSCE 222 with Dr. Carlisle was really enjoyable. His lectures were pretty relevant to the homework problems, and the tests were reasonable as well. Overall, Dr. Carlisle cares for his students a lot and provides a lot of resources to help his students succeed. Definitely looking forward to taking more courses with him in the future.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He expects you to already have full understanding of the language he is teaching. I was also expected to learn a second language unrelated to the class on my own. He doesn't actually ever teach so if you don't understand anything don't expect any help from him. Worst class i have taken so far

Great lectures. Exams and quizzes were pretty easy and tested enough to make sure you actually understand the concept. Homework is the most annoying part, but they shouldnt be too bad. Homework problems are much harder than whats on the exams and quizzes.

Doc's lectures were good. Quizzes and tests were reasonable and only dealt w topics covered in class, no surprises. Wish he did exam reviews, however. HW can be pretty tedious, especially initially bc LATEX. Read the textbook, watch the intro vids, and do the practice problems in the book -> helps a ton w quiz and exam questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Reading and going to lectures is key. The homework can be long and tedious but you learn a lot doing it and it prepares you well for tests. He doesn't give exam reviews but his lectures are pretty thorough, you'll never be surprised. Watching his short videos before class helps a ton, and the textbook is a great help.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Carlisle is the best!CSCE222 was my favorite class this semester; his explanations of all the concepts really worked for me, and I barely needed to study the lecture material because he made it so interesting. Some concepts are only taught via textbook, which didn't always give enough examples, but extra examples can be found easily on the web.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Carlisle clearly shows he wants to help his students understand but the lecture is purely over textbook problems and he calls out on students to answer and if they're right he doesn't explain it to the rest of us or if he does he doesn't go step by step on what you need to do. A lot of my learning was done on my own.

Favorite thing about him is his receptiveness to questions in class. But that leads to my main complaint which is he tends to just do examples of questions in class without explaining them unless you ask him to explain. For some people who don't get the material right away(like me) it can be very frustrating. Tests are fair, quizzes generally easy.

Tests are based on homework, so it's very fair. Homework is a lot of work though, and some of the problems aren't relevant (specifically the ones towards the end). Lectures can be a bit fast, but they're recorded so you can go back. He can be a little blunt and rude at times but is willing to help
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doc is one of the best professors I've had the pleasure of studying under. His lectures can be fast, but he creates short, introductory videos to each topic we discuss before class so you can learn concepts before we do examples. He will explain a concept to you as many times as you ask without judgement. I can't imagine a better prof.
Definitely one of the best professors I've had at A&M. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but he does a great job teaching the class and it was very enjoyable to listen to him.

Prof. Carlisle is simply a good teacher. He teaches very well and gives reasonable hw and exams. If you study, you will get an A almost guaranteed. There are quizzes every week and hw due every week but it's definitely manageable. He doesn't try to trick you and he genuinely wants you to succeed.

Dr Carlisle's class is a lot of fun. He does a brilliant job at keeping the class involved in lectures, despite how info heavy they can be. Quizzes every week, which were completely reasonable. Tests were absolutely fair and had zero surprises. Study the homework and you'll do fine. Overall a great professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really great professor, possibly the most enjoyable instructor I've had in college. He covers all the material that will be on tests and quizzes within his lectures, and makes concepts very simple to understand. His class has consistent, weekly homework that is a little time consuming, but as long as you do the work, an A is easily attainable.

He's goofy most of the lectures he just walks around and calls on ppl which makes it hard to keep up. Doesn't explain things clearly so your're better off watching YT vids/reading. Does not use slides to teach, blank sheet PDF with problems and often does not write work down when teaching. QZs are ez, test are ok. I would take another instructor.
Great Lecturer, class isnt a cakewalk, but its very fair
Hands down the best prof I have had. You can tell he really cares for his students and has very engaging lectures that teach the material and are enjoyable. Take him if you can.

The most caring professor Ive met yet in university. Incredibly kind, compassionate, and intelligent. Has endless time for his students. Changed how I fundamentally thought about computer science, both mathematically and practically. Any lucky student to take his course will be appropriately challenged and engaged.

CSCE 222 is a rough class no matter which professor you take, and I believe Carlisle is the best professor for the class. His lectures take what are normally very complex subjects and bring them down to a level that is pretty understandable no matter your math background. Homework is rough and thick, but I think it's like that for every prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He explains concepts well, but this is a hard class so you should study the book as well. The hw's aren't too long, but you should get started early to finish on time. The quizzes are very straightforward and should be pretty easy and the exams are of the same caliber of the quizzes. If you study the homeworks and the quizzes you should be good.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Goes through lecture quickly, but it's not difficult to pay attention. Gets students to think and ensures everyone is following along. It's a hard class and requires a lot of homework but if you need something explained he will explain it well. Encourages students to work together to solve lecture problems, and similar problems appear on exams/quiz
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: As an honor student, I've had the pleasure of getting amazing profs. On the other hand, this Prof has done nothing to benefit my studies. I've learned most of the material by reading the textbook because he fails to explain the material. He does a lot of examples, speeds through them, and occasionally verbally answers them instead of showing work.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While the lectures can be fast-paced, the doc has flexible office hours and genuinely cares about your grade as much as you do. Homework is plentiful, but if you know the material, it shouldn't be difficult. Quizzes are weekly, but they're short and easy. Tests are challenging if you haven't at least learned easier homework material. Amazing prof!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Hes really nice and funny. He explains the material well.

Doesn't really explain the material, just does examples all lecture and assumes people understand. Grades tough, especially on exams. Don't expect much, if any, partial credit for silly mistakes. Puts the spotlight on random students to answer the question, so learn to think under pressure. Homework is still due on exam weeks. Homework every week.
